title: Wickens wins the Norisring rain race from pole as Vietoris loses second place
dek: Robert Wickens converted pole into a lights-to-flag Norisring win for Mercedes by 23.906 seconds from Jamie Green, while Christian Vietoris lost a wheel when second and Wittmann kept the lead.

chapters.title: Wittmann's home round, Audi in search of a win
text: Round four of ten took the DTM to the Norisring, the 2.3-kilometre street circuit in Nuremberg, and the weekend would draw a crowd of 121,000. It was the home race of Marco Wittmann, who arrived as championship leader after winning in Hungary with 50 points. Mike Rockenfeller was second on 31, 19 behind, with Edoardo Mortara on 27, Adrien Tambay and Miguel Molina on 26 and Christian Vietoris on 25.

Audi, still without a win in 2014, had named the Norisring as the place to change that. Mercedes had won once, through Vietoris in the wet at Oschersleben, and had left Hungary without a point, although its management had said the Norisring should suit the cars.

Practice reflected that mood. Daniel Juncadella was quickest in the first session and Robert Wickens in the second, while the BMW teams struggled in the morning sessions. Rain was forecast for Sunday, which at a street circuit with walls close to the track made the race harder to predict than any of the lap times.

chapters.title: Wickens heads a Mercedes sweep
text: Wickens answered the practice form with a lap of 47.883 seconds to take pole, the first of the year for the Mercedes squad. Paul di Resta was second on 47.976, and Green was the best Audi in third on 47.995, only 0.112 seconds off the top.

Mercedes filled the places behind. Pascal Wehrlein was fourth on 48.008, and Gary Paffett and Vietoris, with the same time of 48.033, were fifth and sixth, so five of the first six cars carried a three-pointed star. Mattias Ekström was seventh on 48.079 and Wittmann eighth on 48.210, the only BMW in the top ten, while Tambay and Nico Müller completed it in ninth and tenth. Ekström's time did not count for as much as it seemed, since he started the race from 12th.

Behind them came Maxime Martin and Rockenfeller, and then Timo Glock, Joey Hand, Farfus and Spengler on the grid from 13th to 16th, with Juncadella 17th, Molina 18th and Tomczyk 19th. Mortara could manage only 20th and Scheider 21st. António Félix da Costa and Tomczyk both failed to get out of Q1, and Vitaly Petrov was last of the 23.

chapters.title: Safety car start and an early penalty
text: A heavy shower just before the start led the race director to send the field away behind the safety car. When the cars were released after the first laps, Wickens pulled away immediately and kept extending his lead.

Behind him the order was shaken up at once. Di Resta, second on the grid, was in contact with Green around the Dutzendteich hairpin early in the race, spun and fell to tenth, and Green took the place. He was given a five-second penalty for the contact. Juncadella also spun after trying to pass Molina and fell to the back of the field.

Green was the only driver who could hold the pace of Wickens, and the pair traded fast laps for a while before the Audi began to fall back. Paffett, Wehrlein and Vietoris ran behind them, and Vietoris gradually worked his way past his team-mates.

chapters.title: A race decided by the switch from wets to slicks
text: The track dried steadily and from around lap 50 the leaders began to move to the option slicks. Spengler was one of the first to come in, and within a few laps most of the field had followed. Wickens stayed out longest, was the last of the leaders to stop at around lap 57, and still came out in front with a lead of about 15 seconds. Vietoris, who had passed Wehrlein and Paffett on the way, jumped Green in the stops and moved into second.

The change of tyres brought the biggest incidents. On lap 58 Tomczyk collided with Paffett, which ended the Schnitzer driver's race and ruined the Mercedes driver's chance of a good result. Farfus, who had stopped early, could not profit from it, and Martin, who had climbed as high as fifth on wets, went back out on wets after his first stop, switched to slicks later and dropped to 17th.

chapters.title: Wickens by 23.906 seconds, Vietoris loses a wheel
text: Wickens took the flag after 82 laps in 1:15:21.118, 23.906 seconds ahead of Green. Vietoris had been running second, but a wheel came loose from his Mercedes close to the end and he fell to 21st in the classification.

That promoted Ekström, who started 12th and rose to third, 25.922 seconds behind, and he set the fastest lap on lap 79. Mortara came from 20th on the grid to fourth, ahead of Wehrlein, who was fifth, and Wittmann was sixth, with Hand seventh and Rockenfeller eighth. Tambay crossed the line fifth after clashing with Wehrlein on lap 69, but was classified ninth, and Timo Scheider completed the top ten a lap behind.
Behind them Spengler was 11th, Paffett 12th, Juncadella 13th, Farfus 14th and di Resta 15th, all a lap down. Glock was 16th, Molina 22nd, eleven laps down, and Tomczyk the only retirement.

chapters.title: Wickens takes the win, Wittmann keeps the lead
text: Wickens said afterwards that he could not have wished for a better day, and that the result, after a hard start to the season, was like a dream. The win was his first of 2014, and he said his aim next was to win a dry race. Mercedes head of DTM marketing Wolfgang Schattling said the team was more than happy and that Wickens had been very quick in all conditions.

Green called second place a good result after the opening-stage penalty, and said he had lost pace on the dry tyres, perhaps because of the pressures. Ekström said he had grown faster as the rain stopped, and that a podium from 12th was fine, although he thought more was possible from seventh. Audi's Dieter Gass said that without Green's penalty the team could have given Wickens a harder fight, but that qualifying had made things difficult.

In the championship Wittmann scored eight points for sixth and kept his lead on 58. Mortara took second place with 39, 19 behind, and Ekström and Rockenfeller were next on 35 each. Tambay had 28 and Molina 26. Wickens and Vietoris were level on 25. Wittmann said the rain tyres wore too quickly for him in the middle of the race, and BMW's Jens Marquardt said sixth and seventh were not what the team had come for but that the damage had been limited. He also praised the spectators who stayed in the stands despite the weather.

For Mercedes it was a mixed evening. Vietoris said the wheel failure had cost him valuable points after he had fought his way to second, and Wehrlein felt fourth place was realistic until Tambay spun him. Paffett said Tomczyk had spun him round, and di Resta, who had started second, felt that the early contact had ruined his afternoon. Schattling noted that with two wins in four races Mercedes had made the best of a hard start. The next round was at Moscow Raceway, with the race on 13 July, and Wehrlein noted that it suited Mercedes less than the Norisring.

facts.v: Wickens won after 82 laps in 1:15:21.118, 23.906 seconds ahead of Green.
